questions.why: The lock file records the exact versions, so every computer installs the same thing.

wrong.0: `npm install` rebuilds it from `package.json` and the lock file.
wrong.1: It holds local values and secrets.
wrong.3: It is build output; the build makes it again.

questions.prompt: `verify.sh` is `npm run lint; echo "verify ok"` with no `set -e`. Lint fails. What happens?
questions.why: `;` runs the next command anyway, and the last command (`echo`) decides the exit code.

wrong.2: The last command is `echo`, which worked, so the code is 0.

questions.prompt: Lint reports an unused variable. What is the best action?
options: Add a comment that switches the rule off
Ignore it; lint is only about style
Remove the variable, or use it if a step is missing
questions.why: Fix the code. An unused variable is often a step you forgot.

wrong.0: That hides the problem; it does not remove it.
wrong.1: Then nothing checks the code at all.
wrong.2: Unused code is often a real mistake, not style.

options: Variable names with empty values, and a comment
Nothing; the file should not exist
questions.why: It is committed, so it tells a newcomer what to set without giving any value away.

wrong.1: It is committed, so real values would be published.
wrong.2: Then nobody knows which variables the project needs.
wrong.3: They are still secrets in spirit, and they get copied into real use.

questions.prompt: GPIS: where should the school's name be written in the code?
options: In every page that shows it
Once, in a config module that other files import
questions.why: One place to change. GPIS keeps it in `src/config/school.ts`.

wrong.0: When it changes, one page will be forgotten.
wrong.2: The app needs it before it has a database connection, for example on a printed page header.

questions.prompt: The README says "run `npm start`". `package.json` has only a `lint` script. What is wrong?
options: The README was never tested: the command does not exist
questions.why: Following the README once, in a fresh copy, would have shown the mistake.

wrong.0: `npm start` works only if a `start` script is defined (or a `server.js` exists).
wrong.1: "How to run" is the most important part of a README.
wrong.2: Renaming hides the mistake. The README should name the real commands.

questions.prompt: `.gitignore` has `.env.*` and no other line about env files. Does `git add .` commit `.env.example`?
options: No; it is ignored until you add a line `!.env.example`
Yes, because it holds no secret
questions.why: `.env.*` matches `.env.example` too. A `!` line makes an exception.

wrong.0: Git has no special rule for example files.
wrong.2: Git does not read file contents to decide what to ignore.
wrong.3: Git never asks; it follows the patterns.
